_comment: Turkish terms chosen for the cultivation lesson batch. status: ok = established in Turkish literature and verified in a source I opened; chosen = my own choice among attested variants; check = only weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. Sources are Turkish-language articles/books I actually opened (see content/research-notes/cultivation.md).

cultivation.note: Project owner fixed “kültivasyon” as main term. ‘ekme’: Yaylagül 2006 (chapter I.F.2 “Kültürel Göstergeler ve Ekme Kuramı”), Erdoğan 1998 (“Gerbner’in ekme tezi”). ‘yetiştirme’: Özer 2005, Ercan & Demir 2015, Özer & Jafarli 2024. ‘ekme-yetiştirme’: Özkan 2017. ‘kültürel göstergeler ve ekme modeli’: title of AUZEF (Polat) unit 8 as given in the project brief (not opened by me).

cultural-indicators.note: Yaylagül 2006, Özer 2005, Ercan & Demir 2015 (abstract: “Kültürel Göstergeler Projesi’nin Kurumsal Süreç Çözümlemesi, Mesaj Sistem Çözümlemesi ve Yetiştirme Çözümlemesi”).

message-system-analysis.note: Ercan & Demir 2015 and Özer & Jafarli 2024 write “mesaj sistem çözümlemesi”; I use the more natural “mesaj sistemi çözümlemesi” in prose and list the attested form as alternative.

cultivation-analysis.note: ‘yetiştirme çözümlemesi’: Özer 2005, Ercan & Demir 2015, Özer & Jafarli 2024. ‘ekme analizi’: Yaylagül 2006. I follow the owner’s ‘kültivasyon’ for the main term.

heavy-viewers.note: Academic Turkish articles I opened write ‘çok izleyenler / çok seyredenler’ (Özer 2005; Erdoğan 1998: “az, orta ve çok”). ‘ağır seyirciler’ appears in the İletişim Ansiklopedisi web entry (yenimedya.info/2020/04/24/cultivation/), not an academic source. ‘ağır izleyici’ chosen for brevity; please confirm with a Turkish reviewer or switch to ‘çok izleyenler’.

light-viewers.note: Same situation as heavy viewers: Özer 2005 and Erdoğan 1998 write ‘az izleyenler’.

cultivation-differential.note: Erdoğan 1998 writes ‘ekme farklılığı’ (percentage difference in TV answers between the two viewer groups). I say ‘kültivasyon farkı’ to stay consistent with the owner’s main term.

mean-world-syndrome.note: ‘kötü dünya sendromu’: Özkan 2017 (Abant Kültürel Araştırmalar Dergisi). ‘Acımasız Dünya Sendromu’: İletişim Ansiklopedisi (yenimedya.info), non-academic. Özer 2005 describes the idea as ‘tehlikeli dünya algısı’ without using a fixed term.

mainstreaming.note: No single fixed Turkish term found. Erdoğan 1998 defines the pattern as ‘ana akım’ (‘anayol, orta yol, ana damar’) and speaks of the ‘ana akım etkisi’; Yaylagül 2006 says media cultivate ‘orta yol değerleri’; Özer & Jafarli 2024 abstract says ‘yetiştirme ve yaygın görüş hâline getirme rolü’ (the last phrase = mainstreaming). ‘ana akımlaşma’ is my own noun for the process, derived from Erdoğan’s ‘ana akım’; the English term is given in parentheses at first mention. FLAGGED for review; core.json note said not to use until sourced — the sources above are now recorded.

resonance.note: Özer 2005 uses the loan word ‘rezonans’ in the title and text and explains it as ‘çifte doz’ etki.

first-order-beliefs.note: Yaylagül 2006 writes ‘ilk düzey etkiler’ and ‘ikincil düzey etkiler’. Potter 1991 (English) speaks of first- and second-order measures.

ceiling-effect.note: Özer 2005 (as reported for Gerbner et al. 1980).

happy-violence.note: Gerbner’s own term (MEF 2010 transcript). The Turkish rendering is mine; the lesson gives the English term in quotation marks next to it.

third-voice.note: Shanahan & Morgan 1999 (Gerbner’s idea of an independent voice between political forces and commercial interests). Own translation.
